decisions.evidence: Maker entry 3/round 2: “Save a link quickly when you come across it.” Client entry 4: “Yes, that captures it.”
decisions.note: Conforming high-level save decision during requirements playback.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 3/round 2: “Organise links with tags.” Client entry 4: “Yes, that captures it.”
decisions.note: Conforming high-level tagging decision during requirements playback.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 3/round 2: “Search to find a link again easily.” Client entry 4: “Yes, that captures it.”
decisions.note: The high-level search decision conforms; detailed search divergences were presented later.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 3/round 2: “Track which links you still intend to read.” Client entry 4: “Yes, that captures it.”
decisions.note: Conforming high-level unread/read-later decision.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 3/round 2: “Keep important links useful even if the original page later changes or disappears.” Client entry 4: preservation is “a safety net.”
decisions.note: Conforming high-level preservation decision; storage-format and PDF behavior were not yet decided.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5/round 3: enter a link and click “Save link”; it appears in “Saved links.” Client entry 6: “the basic ‘save it and it appears in the list’ behaviour matches.”
decisions.note: Conforming prototype save flow.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5/round 3 requires the user to “give it a short title.” Client entry 6: “I’d prefer the title to be filled in automatically from the page when possible, while still letting me change it.”
decisions.note: The initial manual-title requirement conflicts with automatic metadata collection; the client supplied the reference-conforming behavior during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5/round 3 says the form captures exactly “the link address, a title, and an optional…note,” omitting description. Client entry 6 requests automatic title but does not mention the missing editable description.
decisions.note: The explicitly enumerated save/edit data omitted description; the response did not surface that difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5/round 3 presents an optional “why did I save this” note. Client entry 6: “The optional reason is useful.”
decisions.note: A bookmark note is supported; markdown-specific behavior was not established by this decision.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5/round 3 defines item composition as “its title, the site it’s from, and your note,” omitting description, tags, and favicon at that presentation. Client entry 6 approves the basic flow and comments on note and ordering without correcting the composition.
decisions.note: The explicitly presented initial list composition was less complete than the readability-first reference item.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5/round 3: “I chose to show newest links at the top.” Client entry 6: “newest-first works for me.” Neither presentation nor response identifies a user-selectable sort key.
decisions.note: A fixed newest-first ordering was accepted without surfacing the reference expectation that the user can select a sort key.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 7/round 4 presents metadata lookup solely as an automatically filled title. Client entry 8: “that’s exactly the behaviour I want: the title fills itself in.”
decisions.note: The revised prototype collects the title but does not surface automatic description, favicon, or preview-image collection; the response does not identify those missing metadata fields.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 7/round 4 lets the user replace the auto-filled title before saving. Client entry 8 confirms: “I can replace it with something more meaningful before saving.”
decisions.note: Conforming pre-save title override behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 9/round 5: enter multiple tag words and press Enter to create chips. Client entry 10: “Pressing Enter to create tag chips works for me.”
decisions.note: Conforming assignment of one or more tags.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 9/round 5 defines tag entry as typing a word and pressing Enter, calling it the chosen entry style, without offering existing tags as autocomplete. Client entry 10 approves chips and lower-casing but does not request suggestions.
decisions.note: The detailed tag-entry decision omitted existing-tag autocomplete, and the client did not surface the difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 9/round 5 lets the user click a filter-row tag or an item tag to narrow the list. Client entry 10: “clicking a tag to filter the list is enough.”
decisions.note: Conforming specific-tag filtering behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 11/round 6 says search looks “across everything at once” and exhaustively lists title, note, tags, and web address, omitting description. Client entry 12 approves those fields without mentioning description.
decisions.note: The presented full-text field set omitted bookmark descriptions.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 11/round 6 presents bare tag-word search and a simple rule where space-separated words must all occur; no #tag syntax, OR/NOT/parentheses, or exact quoted phrases are included. Client entry 12 says “Requiring all typed words feels sensible” without identifying the richer query-language expectations.
decisions.note: The detailed prototype search semantics were narrower than the reference query language; approval did not explicitly surface or accept those differences.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 11/round 6: “Search and the tag filter work together.” Client entry 12: “search narrowing within the selected tag is the right behaviour.”
decisions.note: Conforming combination of text search and the selected tag filter.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 13/round 7 makes new links “to read” by default and allows changing that state. Client entry 14 confirms the default suits their workflow.
decisions.note: Conforming unread/read-later marking behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 13/round 7 presents “All / To read / Read” views. Client entry 14 approves the “separate views.”
decisions.note: Conforming separate unread-bookmark view.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 13/round 7: “Mark as read” removes the item from the To-read view and it can be flipped back. Client entry 14 approves the read/unread toggle.
decisions.note: Conforming read-state transition.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 15/round 8 presents an opt-in preserved copy, separately viewable inside the app. Client entry 16 explicitly confirms optional per-link copies and separate availability.
decisions.note: Conforming snapshot capability. The prototype’s disclosed simulation is not treated as implementation evidence, and this decision does not establish the PDF edge case.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 15/round 8 says the preserved copy does not replace the normal link. Client entry 16: “the normal link should still open the original page.”
decisions.note: Conforming original-URL navigation decision.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 19/round 10 requires a nonempty valid web address and adds https:// when omitted. Client entry 20 says the messages match expectations and automatic https:// is helpful.
decisions.note: Conforming URL-required save behavior with additional forgiving normalization.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 19/round 10 proposes warning about a duplicate while offering “Save anyway.” Client entry 20: “I’d rather prevent a second copy. The notice should guide me to the bookmark I already saved so I can edit that one instead.”
decisions.note: The client corrected an explicit duplicate-creation path to the reference behavior during edge-case review.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 21/round 11 revises duplicate handling so it is not saved twice and “Go to it” locates the existing bookmark. Client entry 22: “matches what I wanted for duplicates.”
decisions.note: Conforming revised duplicate-save behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 21/round 11 makes title, note, and tags editable and saves changes in place. Client entry 22 does not object to these editable fields.
decisions.note: The individually presented title, note, and tag edit capabilities conform; omitted fields are classified separately.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 21/round 11 explicitly makes the web address non-editable and asks whether it should be changeable. Client entry 22: “I would also expect to edit the web address…so the address shouldn’t be permanently fixed.”
decisions.note: The client extended the presented edit scope with the missing reference-required URL field.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 21/round 11 exhaustively limits editing to “title, note, and tags” while discussing URL separately; description is absent. Client entry 22 requests URL editing but does not mention description editing.
decisions.note: The edit-form presentation omitted post-save description editing, and that distinct omission was not surfaced.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 23/round 12 adds an editable Link address field. Client entry 24 confirms they can “correct or update an address.”
decisions.note: Conforming revised URL-edit capability.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 23/round 12 prevents changing an address to one already used by another bookmark. Client entry 24 confirms duplicates remain prevented.
decisions.note: Conforming duplicate prevention during editing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 25/round 13 presents confirmed permanent removal. Client entry 26: “permanent removal is acceptable once I’ve explicitly confirmed it.”
decisions.note: Conforming permanent-delete behavior; the separate archive capability was not decided in this presentation.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 29/round 15 reports the implemented Save flow. Client entry 30 accepts the software as implementing the approved behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming implementation-review decision for URL saving.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 29/round 15 reports “title fetched automatically from the real page” but no automatic description, favicon, or preview image. Client entry 30 gives bare overall acceptance without identifying the missing metadata.
decisions.note: At implementation review, the presented metadata implementation remained partial; bare approval is not accepted_divergence.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 29/round 15 reports implemented tagging and click-to-filter behavior. Client entry 30 accepts the implementation.
decisions.note: Conforming implemented tag assignment/filtering decision.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 29/round 15 reports search across “title, note, tags and address,” again omitting description. Client entry 30 gives overall acceptance without mentioning the field difference.
decisions.note: The implemented full-text field set remained narrower than the reference at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 29/round 15 reports only that “multiple words narrow” alongside ordinary tag searching; #tag syntax, boolean/parenthesized expressions, literal-operator quoting, and exact quoted phrases are absent from the presented implementation. Client entry 30 gives bare overall acceptance.
decisions.note: The implementation presentation retained the simplified query language, and the response did not surface the difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 29/round 15 reports To-read state, separate All/To-read/Read views, and counters. Client entry 30 accepts the implementation.
decisions.note: Conforming implemented unread workflow.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 29/round 15 reports an opt-in safety-net copy with “real captured page content.” Client entry 30 accepts it and specifically approves graceful handling of unreachable pages.
decisions.note: Conforming implementation-review snapshot decision at the behavior level; the transcript still does not establish the PDF-specific rule.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 29/round 15 exhaustively reports editing “address, title, note and tags,” omitting description. Client entry 30 gives bare overall acceptance.
decisions.note: The implemented edit-field set remained incomplete; bare approval does not show awareness of the missing description field.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 29/round 15 reports “Duplicate prevention with ‘Go to it’.” Client entry 30 accepts the implementation.
decisions.note: Conforming implemented duplicate-save behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 29/round 15 reports removal with a confirmation step. Client entry 30 accepts the implementation.
decisions.note: Conforming implemented delete behavior.
